ModMetadata.Name: IZCode
ModMetadata.Author: julianobd
ModMetadata.Description:
IZCode replaces IC10 with IZ: a structured programming language with types, real functions and recursion, running on its own virtual machine inside the Programmable Chip.
Write '#iz' on the first line of a chip and the mod takes over. Chips without the marker keep working as plain IC10, so nothing you already built changes.
===== WHY IT EXISTS =================================================
IC10 IZ ---- -- 128 lines bounded only by the source size 16 registers, managed by hand named variables, given by the compiler jal/ra, one practical level fn with parameters, returns, recursion restarts every tick freezes and resumes where it stopped an infinite loop hangs the chip preempted by budget, the game carries on typos found at runtime compile errors, with a name suggestion everything is a double num, bool, str, dev checked at compile time HASH("x"), the text is gone a real str: joined, compared, hashed live 16 loose registers struct and arrays, in a real heap
===== A COMPLETE PROGRAM ============================================
#iz device sensor = d0; device inlet = d1; device outlet = d2;
const TARGET = 101.325; const MARGIN = 5.0;
fn main() { loop { var p = sensor.Pressure; inlet.On = p < TARGET - MARGIN; outlet.On = p > TARGET + MARGIN; yield; } }
Execution starts at fn main(); when it returns, the chip stops until restarted.
===== THE LANGUAGE ==================================================
TYPES. num (64-bit float, the one numeric type), bool, str (immutable ASCII), dev (pin d0-d5), T[N] arrays and your own structs. num and bool are NOT interchangeable: 'if x' needs a bool, write 'if x != 0'; the other way round is fine, so 'pump.On = p < 100' works as written.
var counter = 0; // inferred num, mutable var active: bool = false; // explicit annotation const MAX = 101.325; // folded at compile time, free at runtime
Anything declared outside a function is global and keeps its value across ticks.
ARRAYS AND STRUCTS live in the VM heap, laid out entirely at compile time: no allocator to call, nothing to collect.
var samples: num[8]; // eight cells, zeroed struct Gauge { total: num; cursor: num; samples: num[8]; }
The length is part of the type and len(a) folds into a constant. Aggregates travel by reference, so a function fills one in instead of handing it back, and their cells belong to the call that declared them, so recursion gets its own and nothing leaks. An index outside the array stops the chip, and a constant one is caught at compile time.
DEVICES are properties, checked against the game's LogicType table as you type:
device pump = d0; var p = sensor.Pressure; // error if the property does not exist pump.On = true; // error if it is read-only
'Presure' is not a known device property; did you mean 'Pressure'?
BATCH OPERATIONS reach every device on the data network, no cable to each:
all(StructureWallLight).On = true; // by prefab named("Corridor Light").On = false; // by label named(StructureVolumePump, "north").On = true; // both var avg = all(StructureGasSensor).Pressure; // averages; 0 if none
A bare prefab name, a #"hash" literal and a const holding one are all the same compile-time constant, at zero runtime cost.
TEXT is a value like any other: variable, parameter, return, array cell or struct field, and built while the program runs.
var label = "vent-" + side; // == and != compare the text all("Structure" + kind).On = true; // hashed as it runs, the same CRC32 len hash char chr sub find text fixed parse
A num only becomes text through text(x), never silently inside a '+', and hash() of a literal folds at compile time.
CONTROL FLOW: if / else if / else, while, loop, for i in 0..10 (or 0..=10), break, continue. No goto and no labels, braces mandatory, and the range limit is evaluated exactly once.
FUNCTIONS take typed parameters, return a value, may call one declared further down the file, and recurse - bounded by a call depth limit that raises a clean runtime error.
fn gcd(a: num, b: num) -> num { if b == 0 { return a; } return gcd(b, a % b); }
OPERATORS follow C precedence: || && == != < <= > >= | ^ & << >> + - * / %, with -x !x ~x as prefixes. '%' takes the sign of the divisor, as in IC10; division by zero follows IEEE-754. Assignment is a statement, so 'if (a = b)' does not compile, and 'pump.Setting *= 2' works. Math and trigonometry built-ins are all there, plus len, hash, rand, nan and inf.
TICK CONTROL: 'yield' hands the tick back and resumes at the next instruction, 'sleep(2)' suspends for N seconds. Write neither and the VM preempts itself when the budget runs out.
===== THE EDITOR, UPGRADED ==========================================
A REAL CODE AREA. The Stationeers editor is 128 independent text fields, one per line. In IZ mode it becomes one field with a gutter and a current-line highlight: drag selection, Shift+arrows, double click, Ctrl+A/C/X/V, PageUp/PageDown and the wheel all work natively, and indentation follows, VS Code style, down to Tab / Shift+Tab on a whole block.
COMPLETION THAT KNOWS YOUR WIRING. The editor knows which housing is selected and what is wired to each pin, so typing 'pump.' suggests the properties of THAT pump, with the live value alongside, instead of all 358 in the game:
pump. On rw Setting rw = 45 Pressure r = 101.325
It also completes pins, prefab names, slot properties and your own declarations.
ERRORS WHILE YOU TYPE. The same compiler the chip runs on CONFIRM compiles what is on screen a fraction of a second after the last keystroke: red underline for errors, amber for warnings, and a panel saying what is wrong. Runtime errors stop the chip and light the housing's error LED, like an IC10 exception.
HOVER WITH REAL VALUES. Point at a device variable for the equipment, its label, its hash and every readable property; at a #"..." for its hash. Plus syntax highlighting built for IZ, in the editor and on the Motherboard screen.
===== REQUIREMENTS ==================================================
IZCode is a C# plugin, and Stationeers does not load C# on its own: install BepInEx and StationeersLaunchPad first, then enable IZCode in the mods menu. [IZCode] in Player.log confirms it loaded.
Console: 'izcode_devices [rescan]' builds the device catalog and 'izcode_log' controls logging; files live in Documents\My Games\Stationeers\izcode\.
===== SAFE TO TRY ===================================================
Chips without the '#iz' marker behave exactly as they always did. And since '#iz' reads as a comment to the IC10 parser, a chip carrying IZ code does not break the game for someone without the mod installed.
Example programs ship in the samples/ folder: pressure control, solar tracking, batch operations, a moving average, an LED panel, a rolling window, recursion and a full hardsuit controller.
===== MULTIPLAYER ===================================================
Only tested in single player. Multiplayer (a dedicated server or a hosted game) has NOT been tested: every client and the server need the mod installed, and how the VM behaves there is still unknown. Use it at your own risk, and report what you find on the issue tracker below.
